archivedSpeaking.opening: 最初の段の墨線はここに引いてください。軒先の端から測ります。
archivedSpeaking.goal: Show a new worker where to run the first-course chalk line.

curriculumAdaptationNote: Preserve the current first-course layout: tape measure from the eave edge, points associated with the plan, a chalk line for the first shingle row, two workers stretching/snapping it, a straightness check, starter placement along the eave, and the specified overhang measurement on the job plan. Source English/Spanish have a plan-point ambiguity; hold it for source/roofing review. Archived ink-line, generic tier, material strip and eave-projection senses are conditional only. The source curriculum has no authored verb-example list; archived forms remain conditional evidence. No selected learner/audio text or progress identity is created.

cards.reviewNote: Source specifies a chalk line (línea de tiza). Archived 墨線 is an ink line; confirm Japanese chalk-line terminology and avoid changing the layout medium.
First course / primera hilera is the first shingle row; archived 最初の段 may mean a generic stage or tier. Confirm trade wording.
Source pairs starter strip with hilera inicial (starter row). Archived スターター材 names a material; confirm whether a manufactured strip or installed starter course is intended.
Overhang / vuelo del alero is a plan measurement. Archived 軒先の出幅 may mean the eave's building projection rather than the starter/shingle overhang; source/trade decision needed.

cards.sourceEnglish: Run a chalk line for the first course.

cards.archivedEnglish: Run a chalk line for the first course.
cards.reviewNote: Inherits card 1 chalk-versus-ink and card 2 first-course meaning; do not select a layout instruction until both are resolved.

cards.archivedJapanese: 端から測ってください。

reader.sourceSpanish: Primero, el capataz saca la cinta métrica.
reader.sourceEnglish: First, the foreman takes out the tape measure.

reader.archivedEnglish: First, the foreman takes out the tape measure.

reader.sourceSpanish: Mide desde el borde del alero y marca los puntos del plano.
reader.sourceEnglish: He measures from the edge of the eave and marks the points on the plan.
reader.archivedJapanese: 軒先の端から測り、図面に測定点を書き込みます。
reader.archivedEnglish: He measures from the edge of the eave and marks the points on the plan.
reader.reviewNote: Current English says the foreman marks points on the plan after measuring from the eave; source Spanish can mean plan points. Confirm whether the plan or roof surface receives marks before teaching the action.

reader.sourceSpanish: Después dice: Tracen una línea de tiza para la primera hilera.
reader.sourceEnglish: Then he says: Run a chalk line for the first course.

reader.archivedEnglish: Then he says: Run a chalk line for the first course.
reader.reviewNote: Inherits card 9 chalk-line medium and first-course wording questions.

reader.sourceSpanish: Dos obreros estiran la línea y la sueltan.

reader.archivedEnglish: Two workers stretch the line and snap it.
reader.reviewNote: Source says workers stretch and snap the line. Archived 墨つぼの糸 specifies an ink snap line, which conflicts with source chalk/tiza.

reader.sourceSpanish: El capataz revisa la medida otra vez.
reader.sourceEnglish: The foreman checks the measurement again.

reader.sourceSpanish: Pongan la hilera inicial a lo largo del alero.

reader.archivedJapanese: スターター材を軒先に沿って置いてください。

reader.archivedEnglish: The overhang measurement is on the job plan.
reader.reviewNote: The source's overhang measurement is on the job plan; archived 軒先の出幅 may refer to the building eave projection rather than specified shingle/starter overhang.
